newsitem.title: CHINA: China refinery's test output being sold locally.
newsitem.headline: China refinery's test output being sold locally.

text.p: China's largest joint venture oil refinery is producing gasoline and diesel fuel in test operations and marketing the fuel domestically, officials in the venture said on Tuesday.

West Pacific Petrochemical Co Ltd, a joint venture between several Chinese parties and Total SA of France, is also producing naphtha and liquid propane gas at the refinery in northeastern Dalian province, the officials told Reuters.

They declined to give actual output levels but they said four of the refinery's 12 units, including a crude distillation unit and a gas distillation unit, were now in operation and that the others would be brought on stream gradually.
The Dalian venture was designed with a refining capacity of 100,000 barrels of crude oil per day.
A Total official in Beijing said that the test runs, begun at the end of last month, were expected to continue through the end of the year.
After testing is completed, 70 percent of the refinery's output is expected to be exported.
Asian traders have complained that gasoline prices are being depressed by fears that the large refinery will flood the region's markets.
The refinery was originally scheduled to begin operations in May 1995 but technical problems forced delays, according to officials.
Total's partners include Sinochem, Sinopec, the Ministry of Chemical Industry, and the municipal governments of Daqing, site of China's biggest oilfield, and Dalian.
